exampleAnswers.title: Finding Exact Solutions of Exponential Equations

question.text: Given that $3^{x-2} = 5^{4x},$ what is the value of $x?$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
First, we take $\log_3$ on both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} 3^{x-2} &= 5^{4x} \\[3pt] \log_3\left(3^{x-2} \right) & = \log_3\left( 5^{4x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b \left( b^c \right) = c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

\[ x-2 = \log_3\left( 5^{4x}\right). \]

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

\[ x - 2 = 4x\log_3\left( 5\right) \]

Then, we solve for $x,$ as follows: \begin{align} x - 2 & = 4x\log_3( 5)\\[5pt] x & = 2 + 4x\log_3( 5) \\[5pt] x - 4x\log_3( 5) & = 2 \\[5pt] x\left(1 - 4\log_3( 5)\right) & = 2 \\[5pt] x &=\dfrac{2}{1- 4\log_3( 5)} \end{align}

Using the change of base formula, we have \[ \log_3(5) = \dfrac{\ln(5)}{\ln(3)} \approx 1.464\,974. \]

Finally, we can approximate $x$ as \[ x \approx \dfrac{2}{1- 4(1.464\,974)} \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ -0.412}, \] rounded to $3$ decimal places.

question.text: Given that $3^x=2^{x-1},$ what is the value of $x?$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
First, we take $\log_3$ on both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} 3^x&=2^{x-1} \\[3pt] \log_3\left(3^x\right) & = \log_3\left(2^{x-1}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b \left( b^c \right) = c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

\begin{align*} x & = \log_3\left(2^{x-1}\right) \end{align*}

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

\begin{align*} x & = (x-1)\log_3 (2) \end{align*}

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} x & = (x-1)\log_3 (2)\\[5pt] x & = x\log_3(2) - \log_3 (2)\\[5pt] x- x\log_3 (2) & = -\log_3(2) \\[5pt] x(1-\log_3 (2)) &= -\log_3 (2)\\[5pt] x&=-\dfrac{ \log_3 (2)}{1-\log_3 (2)} \end{align*}

Using the change of base formula, we have

\[ \log_3(2) = \dfrac{\ln(2)}{\ln(3)} \approx 0.630\, 930 . \]

Finally, we can approximate $x$ as

\[ x\approx -\dfrac{0.630\, 930 }{1-0.630\, 930 } \approx -1.710 , \]

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.text: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation $e^{x-5}=4^{x}?$
question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{x-5} & =4^{x} \\[3pt] \ln\left(e^{x-5}\right) & = \ln\left(4^{x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

\begin{align*} x-5 & = \ln\left(4^{x}\right) \end{align*}

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

\begin{align*} x-5 & = x\ln 4 \end{align*}

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

\begin{align*} x-5 & = x\ln 4\\[5pt] x-x\ln 4& = 5\\[5pt] x(1-\ln 4) &=5\\[5pt] x&=\dfrac{5}{1-\ln 4} \end{align*}

question.text: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation $e^{x-1}=3^{x}?$
question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{x-1} & =3^{x} \\[3pt] \ln\left(e^{x-1}\right) & = \ln\left(3^{x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

\begin{align*} x-1 & = \ln\left(3^{x}\right) \end{align*}

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

\begin{align*} x-1 & = x\ln 3 \end{align*}

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

\begin{align*} x-1 & = x\ln 3\\[3pt] x-x\ln 3& = 1\\[3pt] x(1-\ln 3) &=1\\[3pt] x&=\dfrac{1}{1-\ln 3} \end{align*}

question.text: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $e^{x+2}=2^{x + 3}.$
question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{x+2} &=2^{x + 3} \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^{x+2}\right) & = \ln \left(2^{x + 3}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

\[ x + 2 = \ln \left( 2 ^{x + 3}\right). \]

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

\[ x + 2 = (x + 3)\ln (2) \]

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} x + 2 & = (x + 3)\ln(2)\\[5pt] x + 2 & = x \ln(2) + 3 \ln(2)\\[5pt] x - x\ln(2) &= 3 \ln(2) - 2 \\[5pt] x (1 - \ln(2)) & =3 \ln(2) - 2 \\[5pt] x & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{3 \ln(2) - 2}{1 - \ln(2)} } \end{align*}

question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} 3^{x+4}&=6^{2-3x} \\[3pt] \ln\left(3^{x+4}\right) & = \ln\left(6^{2-3x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

\begin{align*} (x+4)\ln(3) & = (2-3x)\ln(6) \end{align*}

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

\begin{align*} (x+4)\ln(3) & = (2-3x)\ln(6) \\[5pt] x\ln(3)+4\ln(3) & = 2\ln(6)-3x\ln(6) \\[5pt] x\ln(3)+3x\ln(6) & = 2\ln(6)-4\ln(3) \\[5pt] x\left(\ln(3)+3\ln(6)\right) & = 2\ln(6)-4\ln(3) \\[5pt] x & = \dfrac{2\ln(6)-4\ln(3)}{\ln(3)+3\ln(6)} \end{align*}

question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} 3^{2x}&=8^{1-6x} \\[3pt] \ln\left(3^{2x}\right) & = \ln\left(8^{1-6x}\right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

\begin{align*} 2x\ln(3) & = (1-6x)\ln(8) \end{align*}

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

\begin{align*} 2x\ln(3) & = (1-6x)\ln(8) \\[5pt] 2x\ln(3) & = \ln(8)-6x\ln(8) \\[5pt] 2x\ln(3)+6x\ln(8) & = \ln(8) \\[5pt] 2x\left(\ln(3)+3\ln(8)\right) & = \ln(8) \\[5pt] x & = \dfrac{\ln(8)}{2\left(\ln(3)+3\ln(8)\right)} \end{align*}

question.text: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $3^{4-x}=8^{2x+3}.$
question.explanation:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation: \begin{align*} 3^{4-x}&=8^{2x+3} \\[5pt] \ln\left(3^{4-x}\right) & = \ln\left(8^{2x+3} \right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives \[ (4-x)\ln(3) = (2x+3)\ln(8). \]

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows: \begin{align*} (4-x)\ln(3) & = (2x+3)\ln(8)\\[5pt] 4\ln(3)-x\ln(3) & = 2x\ln(8)+3\ln(8) \\[5pt] -x\ln(3) - 2x\ln(8) & = 3\ln(8)-4\ln(3) \\[5pt] x\ln(3) + 2x\ln(8) & = 4\ln(3)-3\ln(8) \\[5pt] x\left(\ln(3)+2\ln(8)\right) & = 4\ln(3)-3\ln(8)\\[5pt] x & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{4\ln(3)-3\ln(8)}{\ln(3)+2\ln(8)}} \end{align*}
